keyFacts: A personal loan is unsecured: no collateral, so the lender charges a higher rate for the risk.
EMI stays fixed for the whole tenure on a fixed-rate personal loan.
Typical tenures run 1 to 5 years; longer tenures lower the EMI but raise total interest.
Processing fees of 1 to 3% and GST are usually added on top of the interest.
Prepayment or foreclosure charges may apply if you close the loan early.
Your credit score largely decides the rate you are offered.

personal-loan-calculator.formula:
EMI = P x r x (1 + r)^n / ((1 + r)^n - 1).
P = loan amount, r = monthly rate (annual rate / 12), n = months.
Total interest = (EMI x n) - P.
Example: 200,000 at 11% for 36 months: r = 0.009167, EMI = 6,547.74, total interest = 35,719.
personal-loan-calculator.workedExample:
Loan 200,000, annual rate 11%, tenure 3 years:
1. Monthly rate: 0.11 / 12 = 0.009167; months = 36.
2. EMI: 200,000 x 0.009167 x 1.009167^36 / (1.009167^36 - 1) = 6,547.74.
3. Total paid: 6,547.74 x 36 = 235,719.
4. Total interest: 235,719 - 200,000 = 35,719.
Shortening to 2 years would cut interest to about 23,389 with an EMI of 9,308.

faqs.q: Why is the personal loan rate higher than a home loan rate?
faqs.a: Because there is no collateral. If you default on a home loan, the lender can sell the house; on a personal loan it has no asset to recover, so it prices that risk into a higher interest rate.

faqs.q: Should I choose a longer tenure for a lower EMI?
faqs.a: Only if you need the breathing room. A longer tenure always costs more total interest. A good rule: pick the shortest tenure whose EMI you can pay comfortably even in a bad month.

faqs.q: What is a good interest rate for a personal loan?
faqs.a: It depends on your credit score and market. Strong scores often get 10 to 14%, average scores 14 to 18%, and weak scores higher. Compare the total interest across offers, not just the rate.

faqs.q: Does prepaying a personal loan save money?
faqs.a: Yes, usually. Paying principal early cuts the balance that future interest is charged on. Check the prepayment or foreclosure charge first: if it exceeds the interest you would save, wait.

faqs.q: How does my credit score affect the loan?
faqs.a: Lenders use it to price risk. A higher score means a lower offered rate and faster approval. Even a 2% lower rate on a large loan saves a meaningful amount, which is why protecting your score matters.

faqs.q: EMI vs total interest: which should I optimize?
faqs.a: Both, in order: first make sure the EMI fits your monthly budget with margin, then minimize total interest by choosing the shortest comfortable tenure and the lowest rate you can get.
